svg.title: Review an imported API before you deploy it
svg.desc: Five steps read top to bottom. 1, take an inventory of a local OpenAPI 3.1 document in JSON or YAML: --list shows every operation with a verdict and its reasons, and no remote call is made. 2, review an explicit policy that --init-policy scaffolds with the origin, authentication, effects, statuses and limits; relaxations are named and reported, and the importer guesses none of these decisions. 3, every selected operation is checked: if one is unsupported the import is rejected with a code and source pointer and nothing is written, and generated Actions must compile before any file is written; otherwise revise the document or policy, or write a custom adapter. 4, review the generated files: with --target builtin, Actions on weave-http@2.0.0, a connection example with secret-handle placeholders, and provenance; with --target package, the default, a connector package to build. 5, deploy through the normal gates: built-in Actions are published, then a connection is created and the workflow activated; a package is built, installed, allowlisted, published and activated; release admission, grants and connection pins still apply. Import stays offline and allocates no live IDs.
svg.text: Review an imported API before you deploy it
Import only shapes local files. Publication, credentials, and runtime
admission come later, through the usual gates.
READ DOWN • Each arrow carries the result into the next step
1. Take an inventory of the document
Use a local OpenAPI 3.1 document in JSON or YAML.
--list shows every operation with a verdict and its reasons.
INPUT • No remote API call is made
2. Review an explicit policy
--init-policy scaffolds the origin, authentication, effects,
statuses, and limits. Relaxations are named and reported.
POLICY • The importer does not guess these decisions
3. Check every selected operation
If any selected operation is unsupported, the import is
rejected with a code and source pointer; nothing is written.
Generated Actions must compile before any file is written.
Revise the document or policy, or write a custom adapter.
NO → Revise and repeat • YES → Review generated output
4. Review the generated files
--target builtin: Actions on weave-http@2.0.0, a connection
example with handle placeholders, and provenance.
--target package (default): a connector package to build.
Compare configuration, schemas, authentication, and effects.
REVIEW • Generated does not mean approved
5. Deploy through the normal gates
Built-in: publish the Actions → create a connection → activate.
Package: build → install → allowlist → publish → activate.
Release admission, grants, and connection pins still apply.
DEPLOY • Provider onboarding remains separate
Import remains an offline operation
It allocates no live resource IDs and makes no provider request. Treat the
generated files as reviewable starting material.

g.text: Imported metadata is a starting point for review, not permission to run.
